clues: This city stands where a river valley cuts the edge of the high plains. A great wall of rocky peaks rises just west of its streets.
Winter here swings between deep snow with bitter cold and mild, soft days. Warm winds, called Chinooks, slide in and break the cold spell.
This gold town won the chief job for its territory in 1867. In 1881, a vote of the whole state made it the state capital for good.
Outside the west door of the capitol, the fifteenth step is carved with words that name its height. Stand on that step and you stand one full mile high.
The laws of Colorado are made in this city. It is the state capital, and the state's largest city too.
